title: 2026-07-25 Redwood migration demo: OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood (parity mapping)
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-07-25
Time: 16:00 - 16:45 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE); Maria Gonzalez (CTO - Novum Health), Samir Patel (Lead ML Eng), Elena Brooks (SRE)
summary: Demo focused on parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API; discussed API mapping, embeddings differences, streaming & function-calling equivalence, security (SOC2/KMS/VPC), and benchmarking plan.
transcript:
00:00 Alex Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we are at 4 pm PDT, will run 45 minutes, quick intros
00:07 Maria Gonzalez: thanks alex, i'm maria CTO at Novum Health, Samir and Elena on call
00:12 Alex Chen: great thanks Maria, i'm alex chen (ae) at Redwood, with Priya our se
00:18 Priya Patel: hi all, i'll do most of the demo, hope to cover the api parity and console
00:27 Samir Patel: quick ask - we use OpenAI's streaming + function call heavily, also Anthro- pic models, and Together for some high throughput batch jobs
00:40 Priya Patel: perfect, that's exactly what we'll map. quick agenda: api mapping, console, optimize suggestions, security
00:50 Alex Chen: also we'll show how to set up dedicated vs hosted, and pilot benchmarks
01:12 Priya Patel: (screen) starting with api -> Redwood exposes a text generation endpoint /v1/generate that's very similar to openai completion/chat but with small differences. for streaming you can hit the same endpoint with ?stream=true, or use our websocket streaming
01:35 Maria Gonzalez: how about role tokens? we have chat messages with roles user/system/assistant
01:42 Priya Patel: yes we preserve roles; we map openai messages array to messages param, anthro's chat format maps to the same. there are slight differences in stop tokens handling - reedwood (sic) will accept stop sequences as string or array, sometimes the transcription shows 'reedwood' instead of 'redwood'
01:58 Samir Patel: and function calling? we do auto call with a schema
02:05 Priya Patel: we support function calls - same idea: send function schema, and model will return call structured output; note: some older together models don't support function_call natively, we fallback to structured output postprocessing
02:25 Elena Brooks: ok, got to ask about embeddings - we run semantic search indexing in prod, how do embeddings parity look? tokenization differences cause drift
02:36 Priya Patel: good q - we have curated embeddings models and mapping table. OpenAI 'text-embedding-3-small' roughly maps to redwood-embed-small, anthropic embeddings map similarly. we recommend running sample comparisons - cosine drift expected ~0.01-0.03 in many cases, sometimes higher with domain-specific docs
02:55 Alex Chen: on quantization - for dedicated we can provision int8 models, cost down 2-3x depending on perf. Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles per workload
03:12 Samir Patel: latency/cost tradeoff - our SLA needs 200ms p95 for short chats
03:18 Priya Patel: we discussed routing - latency-first routing will pick faster instance types and smaller models; you can also pin to dedicated capacity to guarantee throughput
03:30 Maria Gonzalez: security - SOC2, SAML, KMS, what do you provide? our compliance team needs audit logs and customer-managed keys
03:40 Alex Chen: we have SOC2 reports, SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs; private deployments support BYOK via KMS/HSM and VPC peering for on-prem
03:55 Elena Brooks: data retention and delete requests?
04:00 Priya Patel: you can configure retention policies per route; hosted by default 30 days but can set to 0-retain with private
04:18 Samir Patel: curious about KV cache and prefix caching - we use prefix caching to speed up repeated prompts
04:25 Priya Patel: Redwood runtime has KV caching; we support pinned cache keys per customer and automatic prefix caching in Redwood Optimize suggestions
04:42 Maria Gonzalez: great. next, console walkthrough
04:45 Priya Patel: (narrating) here is the console, route creation, model mapping, set credits, set scale policies, health graphs, token cost breakdowns
05:10 Samir Patel: can we see per-team usage and per-route tracing?
05:15 Priya Patel: yes RBAC + per-route dashboards, traces link to the raw transcript and cost buckets
05:30 Maria Gonzalez: can you show how to migrate a simple chat flow? we have a microservice currently calling openai.com/v1/chat
05:45 Priya Patel: sure - mapping: messages -> messages, temperature, top_p same; for model names map gpt-4 -> redwood-gpt4-1 compat or open weights equivalent; for streaming set stream flag; for function calls keep schema payload the same but change endpoint + auth header
06:05 Samir Patel: any code sample? will you share a migration snippet
06:12 Priya Patel: yes we'll share a parity mapping sheet and code snippets, also a demo repo. quick snippet: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDWOOD_KEY' -d '{"model":"redwood-gpt4-1","messages":...}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
06:30 Maria Gonzalez: embeddings migration - we need to reindex; how do we keep search consistency during rollout?
06:38 Priya Patel: two options: shadow indexing (run both embeddings and compare) or do a phased re-index with canary tests; Redwood Optimize can run sample evals and flag regressions
06:50 Alex Chen: about benchmarking - we recommend a 48-72 hour pilot with a subset of traffic. Priya will run perf tests and share results
07:05 Samir Patel: what about request signing and rate limits? we have throttles
07:10 Priya Patel: rate limits per key by default; Dedicated can raise limits and you get quotas; request signing via certs for private
07:20 Elena Brooks: integration with our infra - we use K8s and service mesh, any special networking for private?
07:28 Alex Chen: private deployments support VPC peering, private link, or on-prem docker/k8s packages, our SD team helps set up peering and routes
07:42 Maria Gonzalez: any gotchas moving from Together models - we used Together for high throughput cheaply
07:48 Priya Patel: Together models sometimes have slightly different tokenization and context window behavior; also model api params differ; we'll include Together-specific notes in parity sheet
08:05 Samir Patel: what about cost models - can we get per-token cost projections for our workload
08:12 Alex Chen: yes we'll run a cost projection using your sample workload and present options hosted vs dedicated vs private with numbers
08:25 Priya Patel: Optimize will recommend batching, cache TTLs, and quantization profiles; typical ROI 20-40% cost savings depending on workload
08:45 Maria Gonzalez: okay, security vetting - our legal wants SOC2 report and data flow diagram
08:52 Alex Chen: i'll share SOC2 report and an architecture diagram; security packet link will be provided
09:02 Priya Patel: moving on to action items and pilot steps - propose spin up a dedicated trial with sample traffic 48 hrs
09:10 Maria Gonzalez: sounds good, timeline: we want a pilot in two weeks, aim for Aug 8th
09:18 Alex Chen: noted. last q - any limitations with function calls and streaming together?
09:24 Priya Patel: some older models stream differently; we recommend a small compatibility test; function-calls during stream are supported but you may see chunked json that needs recombining
09:40 Samir Patel: any per-route model rollback options?
09:44 Priya Patel: yes rollouts: canary and automatic fallback policies to previous model or to cheaper variant
09:56 Alex Chen: recap and next steps
10:00 Alex Chen: recap: we'll share parity sheet, demo repo, SOC2, architecture diagram; Priya will run a pilot benchmark and Samir will share sample traffic
10:15 Maria Gonzalez: thanks everyone, looking forward to the pilot
10:20 Alex Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and artifacts
10:30 (call ends) - transcription notes: minor ASR errors, some product name misspellings (reedwood) and occasional speaker mislabels

Priya to run pilot benchmark (48-72h) starting the week of 2026-08-03 and share results

Alex to share SOC2 report and security packet by 2026-07-27
Schedule pilot kickoff meeting for week of 2026-08-03
